clue.text: To doctor, evidence of his failure?

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A wry remark addressed to a physician: his patients' graves show where his treatment went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a doctor's failed treatment ends up buried in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave marker is the grim result when a physician's patient dies, so it testifies to his lack of success.

clue.text: Event in which the first over the line are the losers

definitions.text: Event in which the first over the line are the losers

parts.words: Event in which the first over the line are the losers
parts.note: in a rope-pulling contest the team dragged across the centre mark loses, unlike a race where crossing first wins

explanation.surface: Sounds like a perverse race where crossing the finish first means defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a running race; in this contest the team pulled over the line loses.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rope-pulling contest, the side hauled over the marked line has been beaten.

clue.text: Saw a little marmot today

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reports spotting a small marmot this very day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past tense of see; here it is the noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a guiding phrase.

clue.text: After turning up, one jostling is an easy target

indicators.note: after says the jostler comes behind the turned word
turning the little word 'up' round makes it read backwards

parts.note: someone who jostles is a shover

explanation.surface: Someone who pushes their way upward in a crowd proves easy to knock over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word for the whole scene, but it only orders the two pieces; 'turning' acts on 'up' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or opponent easily beaten or persuaded is called by this informal term.

clue.text: Illegal to be totally drunk

definitions.meaning: dealings done secretly and unlawfully are said to be done this way, out of sight
someone so intoxicated they have collapsed to the floor below the furniture

explanation.surface: A comment that being utterly intoxicated ought to be against the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden payments are made covertly, out of sight; a very drunk person has slumped to the floor.

clue.text: Bird swimming in Rhone

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird paddling in the French river Rhône.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges RHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird of riverbanks, a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Dracula maybe in rage chasing seductive woman

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the rage word comes after the woman

parts.note: a vamp is a woman who uses her charms to seduce
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Count Dracula, perhaps furious, pursuing an alluring woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the most famous example of a blood-drinking undead creature; 'maybe' signals an example.

clue.text: Black bird in castle

definitions.meaning: a dark-plumaged crow-family bird that nests in colonies
the chess piece also called a castle

explanation.surface: A dark bird nesting in a castle's battlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' is the chess piece, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a black crow-like bird and the chess piece shaped like a tower.

clue.text: A jacket almost on fire

indicators.note: almost says the jacket word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a blazer is a kind of jacket

explanation.surface: A jacket that is nearly burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of BLAZER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burning fiercely with flames is described as on fire.

clue.text: Retire? That might be good bet

indicators.note: might be says these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A tip that retiring could be a sound wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges GOOD BET.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire at night means turning in to sleep; the question mark flags this sense rather than leaving work.

clue.text: Lover put small jumper round me

indicators.note: round says the jumper word goes around the other piece

parts.note: roo is a short word for kangaroo, a jumping animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweetheart wraps a little sweater around the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater; it is a kangaroo, and 'small' shortens it to ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo is the archetypal ardent young suitor, so his name stands for any amorous man.

clue.text: All the flowers are for her

definitions.text: All the flowers are for her

parts.words: All the flowers are for her
parts.note: the Roman goddess of blossoms; her name also means all the plant life of a region

explanation.surface: Sounds like a lover giving every bouquet to one woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'her' is the Roman goddess of flowers, whose name also means a region's plant life.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of blossoms gives her name to the whole plant life of an area.

clue.text: Worked with detectives to get rank

parts.note: ran, as in operated a machine or managed a business
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Someone collaborated with police detectives to earn a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a noun for position; here it is an adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank and this word both describe food that smells sour and spoiled.

clue.text: Perhaps one may risk speaking

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
to dare is to venture or risk
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: Someone might take a chance by speaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild way of conceding a possibility, much like saying probably or maybe.

clue.text: In most dangerous position, in ship's bow?

definitions.meaning: idiom for being where the difficulties or danger are greatest
a ship's bow is its pointed front end, jokingly the pointy end

explanation.surface: Facing peril, standing right in the prow of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the place of greatest risk; literally, the front of a vessel is its pointed end.

clue.text: Difficulty replacing our belt

indicators.note: replacing means putting the letters back in different places

explanation.surface: Having a hard time getting a new belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges OUR BELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble and difficulty are synonyms for a problem or hardship.

clue.text: Edit socialist law

parts.note: red is a common label for a left-winger or socialist
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: An instruction to amend a left-wing statute.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to revise or censor a text before publication, a kind of editing.

clue.text: Escort struggling to show restraint

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A minder fighting to show self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges ESCORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight laced undergarment confines the body, so it is literally a restraint.

clue.text: Sort of boom very pleasant, having no end

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: having no end says the pleasant word loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: An economic boom that is very pleasant and never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no end' cuts NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonic boom is the bang caused by an aircraft exceeding the speed of sound, so the word describes that kind.

clue.text: Artist expected resistance capturing king

indicators.note: capturing means holding the king letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon
R, from rex, Latin for king
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A painter anticipated opposition when seizing a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts R (king) inside DUER.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and printmaker.

clue.text: Where to be rescued from severe habit?

definitions.text: Where to be rescued from severe habit?

indicators.note: rescued from says the answer is pulled out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asks where an addict can go to be saved from a bad dependency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rescued from' extracts letters across 'severe habit'; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic for treating addiction is where someone escapes a damaging habit, short for rehabilitation.

clue.text: Youngster saves pounds for such fiction?

indicators.note: saves means holding the pounds letter safe inside the youngster word

parts.note: a pup is a young dog or a cheeky youngster
L, from libra, the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: A young person putting money aside to buy cheap novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saves' puts L inside PUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid cheap novels and magazines printed on rough paper are known as pulp fiction.

clue.text: No time for headdress in town

indicators.note: no says the time letter is absent from the headdress

parts.note: a turban is a wrapped cloth headdress

explanation.surface: Someone without time to fetch a headdress while in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes T from TURBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban describes things belonging to or located in a city, as opposed to the countryside.

clue.text: God, support us when we speak

indicators.note: when we speak says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: back us means support us

explanation.surface: A prayer asking a deity to stand behind us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when we speak' says BACK US is heard, giving the god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine and revelry.

clue.text: Having power, makes contact in lectures

indicators.note: having says the contact word holds the power letter at its front

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to reach someone is to get in touch with them

explanation.surface: A powerful speaker connects with the audience during talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lectures' looks like a noun; it is a verb, to moralise at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone is to moralise or sermonise at them at length.

clue.text: Conform to orders, being extra yielding at first

indicators.note: at first means taking the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Following commands means being especially compliant from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conform to orders' looks like the whole definition, but 'orders' gives its first letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: To do as you are told is to comply or fall into line with rules.
